chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked, 'What is the al-muhsan?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'May Allah have mercy on you. The one who has a woman for whom he goes out in the morning and returns in the evening, so he is al-muhsan.'

key_terms.الْمُحْصَنُ: The married person (specifically one eligible for stoning)
key_terms.وَيَرُوحُ: And he returns to her in the evening
key_terms.يَغْدُو عَلَيْهِ: He goes to her in the morning

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a married man (muhsan) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential definition of 'al-muhsan' (the married person liable for stoning) by emphasizing the existence of a consummated marital bond with regular conjugal access. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that mere contract is insufficient; the key criterion is the practical reality of a wife over whom the husband has rights of intimacy, distinguishing this status from simple betrothal. This definition is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining the application of hadd al-rجم in cases of zina.
